title: Model-agnostic harness: local models and cloud providers
objective: Keep the harness model-agnostic while supporting native provider authentication from the guest where the harness actually runs. OpenCode ChatGPT login must use a currently supported browser-based flow with its callback reaching the real guest OpenCode server; optional secure host escrow/import/export must not replace or block native login. Keep secrets out of the image, workspace, seed and Git.

acceptance_criteria.text: A default launch with no cloud credentials works against the host-side ollama/llamacpp API reached through the narrow guestfwd channel, exactly as the no-subscription path requires.

Provider configuration is generated by scripts/regen-configs for at least one cloud provider end to end, and documented for Kimi, Claude and OpenAI; adding a provider never requires hand-editing a generated file.

Cloud credentials, including saved OAuth accounts, are supplied at runtime from a host-only credential escrow or keychain and never baked into the image, cloud-init ISO, shared base image, workspace, or Git; git status is clean after a session and image/seed inspection finds no secrets.
A single config or environment switch selects local versus cloud without changing the workspace command; ./lab <dir> stays the same.
Cloud provider domains are added to the egress allowlist only for the selected provider, and removed when switching back to local.
Failure modes are actionable: missing key, egress denied and provider outage each give a clear message; local fallback is documented and needs no code change.
Tests cover config generation, secret non-persistence, one provider call (live or stubbed) and an egress-denied cloud call.

A documented VM configuration option controls credential forwarding with secure defaults: `off` imports nothing, `auto` imports every supported credential found in the host escrow, and an explicit provider list imports only named integrations. The configuration contains selectors/paths only, never secret values.

With forwarding enabled and a supported host credential available, a fresh disposable VM starts the agent already connected without another browser login or pasted key. OpenAI ChatGPT Plus is proven via OpenCode `auth export`/`auth import`; API-key providers such as Anthropic/Kimi use their supported runtime credential mechanism.

OpenCode's data directory is persisted outside the agent container's `/home/agent` tmpfs for the VM lifetime, and `lab-vm stop/down` securely exports refreshed OAuth state back to the host escrow atomically before deleting the overlay. A failed export does not silently destroy the last usable credential state.

Credential forwarding is provider-agnostic, auditable without logging secrets, uses the existing SSH control channel or an equivalent non-workspace channel, preserves mode 0600/0700, and exposes no broad host credential directory to the VM.

Fresh VM supports a currently supported non-device-code OpenCode ChatGPT browser OAuth login (including Sign in with ChatGPT/token-sharing if offered), not only device code: discover actual methods/version and callback location, open URL in host browser, route required callback across host→VM→agent/server through a temporary loopback-only SSH forward, verify auth list and one provider request. For pinned OpenCode 2.2.0, derive the OS-selected callback port from the actual OAuth redirect_uri rather than assuming a fixed port; this integration is confirmed by source inspection, not a stable CLI/API contract, and must be rechecked on version changes. Repeat with device code unavailable; no API-key substitution or broad/LAN port exposure.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Owner CachyOS report: browser reached host Firefox but returned to 127.0.0.1:40391, while prior SSH trace showed only fixed listeners 1455/1457; this is consistent with the pinned v2.2.0 provider source calling server.listen(0, 127.0.0.1). Local follow-up derives the exact redirect_uri port and adds one loopback SSH control-master forward before opening the unchanged URL. Callback, auth list, and provider request remain unverified live.

acceptance_criteria.text: Human auth gate is planned and fed back through the engine before container/VM teardown: export existing login privately first; test browser callback success/cancellation/occupied port, egress denied, container recreation, VM deletion/re-import and refreshed token persistence. Record redacted results and exact version/method; never log URL state, codes or tokens.

OpenAI browser sign-in is a smooth single-command host workflow: one explicit command starts the native guest OpenCode browser OAuth flow, derives the actual callback port from the validated runtime redirect_uri, establishes only that temporary host/guest loopback SSH forward, and opens the unchanged authorization URL in the host browser without a second manually coordinated terminal or URL copy. It closes temporary forwarding on success, cancellation, interruption, timeout, and failure; remains the browser method (not device code); and never logs/stores the authorization URL, state, code, or tokens. Runtime redirect_uri parsing is source-dependent rather than a stable OpenCode API and must fail closed if its expected shape changes.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Owner live attempt failed at host Firefox 127.0.0.1:40391 because implementation had fixed 1455/1457 forwards. Source-level diagnosis and a narrow dynamic-forward implementation are now present with local tests and documentation; owner acceptance is still pending.

acceptance_criteria.text: A host-resident browser-bridge MCP integration lets the guest-started native OAuth flow open its authorization URL in the host's default browser without manual URL copy/paste. The bridge is a narrowly scoped open-auth-URL capability, bound to host loopback and reachable only through the per-VM SSH channel; it accepts only approved provider authorization origins, provides no arbitrary host command/file/network access, does not receive or relay the OAuth callback/code, and never logs or persists authorization URLs, state, codes, or tokens. For pinned OpenCode 2.2.0 it extracts only the validated runtime redirect_uri port, adds exactly one host-loopback→guest-loopback SSH control-master forward before opening the unchanged URL, and closes it with the master. This relies on inspected provider source, not a stable CLI/API contract; version changes must be rechecked and unexpected URL shapes fail closed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local implementation and regression tests cover the source-derived 127.0.0.1 callback, port validation, exact loopback SSH control forward and forwarding-before-browser order. The 2026-10-29 owner attempt showed port 40391 and failed under the former fixed-port setup; successful live callback/cleanup remain pending.

acceptance_criteria.text: First-login milestone: from the normal guest OpenCode TUI, native non-device-code ChatGPT browser OAuth completes its callback to the actual guest server, saves the account in the intended private credential store, and supports `opencode auth list` plus a real provider completion. One explicit owner approval is the only interactive step; no second terminal or manual URL transfer is required.

Workspace-start milestone: after selecting/connecting Little Mester to workspace X, the standard documented start workflow has all required auth configuration present. If no credential exists, it guides or launches the one-time native TUI login; after that, ordinary workspace starts reuse the saved auth without extra setup or repeated login.

Credential handling supports explicitly enabled recursive Little Mester use: prefer private app/OS credential storage outside the worktree; any workspace-local fallback is Git-ignored, mode-restricted, and excluded from commits, images, build contexts, and logs. Auth is forwarded only at runtime through a narrow secret channel to nested Little Mester containers, without copying a broad credential directory or requiring reauthentication; a nested end-to-end test proves this while preserving existing recursion bounds.

#45 browser auth human gate after #41 provisioning passes: list opencode auth methods/version without starting an unattended login; implement loopback-only callback transport to the actual server namespace, test provider login/call with device flow disabled, then persistence/teardown. Requires owner browser interaction; remain pending until observed.

Sequence per parent #35 A21: native VM browser auth and persistence is a required gate before moving actual work to the VM; it follows successful local model connectivity and core guest TUI checks. Existing host-Docker auth remains the rollback and is not proof of VM auth. Do not copy the Docker OpenCode database into the guest or recreate the existing host container. Run the browser callback/cancel/occupied-port/provider-call/restart-persistence handoff only in the VM and keep secrets redacted/private.

NEXT OWNER GATE (#45 A12/A13): preserve the working host-Docker session and current VM overlay; do not run `up --clean`, stop, down, recreate the host container, or alter firewall/network settings. Terminal 1: `./lab-vm -d agent`. Terminal 2: `./lab-vm auth-forward` (host loopback ports 1455/1457 must be free; helper should stay attached). In the guest TUI use `/connect` → OpenAI → its browser OAuth method, not device code; open the displayed auth URL in the host browser and complete the owner's normal approval. After success, confirm `opencode auth list` reports OpenAI stored and make one harmless OpenAI completion. Press Ctrl-C in the auth-forward terminal after success so the loopback tunnel closes. Do not copy or print the URL, state, code, or token. Report only version, method label, success/error, auth-list state, completion result, and whether the tunnel exited.

Then test cancellation without completing approval and confirm the helper is stopped after cancellation; test occupied host callback port(s) and verify `auth-forward` fails closed with no listener exposed; test denied OpenAI egress in a disposable workspace/policy, not by weakening or unexpectedly editing the live workspace policy. Preserve any existing saved credentials. Container recreation, VM deletion/re-import, refreshed-token persistence, and credential escrow are separate pending gates; do not claim A3/A9/A10/A13 passing without those results.

Diagnose and safely restore the current VM host egress proxy on its recorded loopback port without restarting QEMU or changing/deleting the overlay. Verify the process identity/version before signaling; reload/restart only the host proxy safely, preserve the selected workspace policy, and validate guest egress after recovery.

Replace the manual `agent` + separate `auth-forward` + copied URL sequence with one host command that orchestrates the native OpenCode browser method, host browser launch/handoff, callback forwarding, cancellation/timeout cleanup, and actionable failure handling. No device-code fallback may be presented as satisfying the browser gate.

Owner acceptance after recovery: one-command native browser login succeeds; repeat cancellation/interruption; verify occupied callback port fails closed; verify denied OpenAI egress; check guest `opencode auth list` and one completion; preserve host-Docker session and overlay. Do not record OAuth URL/state/code/token.

Prototype and threat-model a host-side browser-bridge MCP tool callable by the guest only over the existing per-VM SSH control channel. Demonstrate it opens only allowlisted provider authorization origins in the host default browser, has no generic host tool capability, keeps URL/state in memory only, and does not intercept callback codes/tokens.

Integrate browser-bridge invocation into the single-command native auth flow; test unreachable host bridge, unsupported provider origin, browser-launch failure, cancellation, timeout, and cleanup without exposing a LAN service or requiring a second manually coordinated terminal.

CURRENT OWNER GATE (supersedes prior separate `agent` + `auth-forward` + manual URL handoff): first complete #41's proxy-recovery gate without restarting QEMU or changing host network/firewall state. Preserve the current VM/overlay and host-Docker session. Run `./lab-vm auth`; in guest `/connect` → OpenAI → its browser OAuth method (not device code). Verify automatic host-browser opening and guest callback success; if the pinned build does not call the shim or the browser does not open, stop—never copy/paste the URL as workaround. On success, verify guest `opencode auth list` and one harmless OpenAI completion. Also cancel a separate attempt, exit OpenCode, and verify cleanup of bridge, token/helper, and SSH forwards. Report only version/method, success/cancel/error, auth-list/completion outcomes, and cleanup; never record URL/state/code/token. Keep the existing VM/overlay and host-Docker session; do not run `--clean`, stop/down, or recreate containers.

After the basic owner flow, separately test occupied callback port(s) fail closed, denied OpenAI egress, interruption/startup-failure cleanup, and timeout behavior. The current command waits for the interactive TUI and relies on exit/signal cleanup; no independent OAuth-cancellation detector or timeout acceptance is claimed. Persistence/export/import, container recreation, and VM deletion remain separate pending gates.

CALLBACK FAILURE follow-up (supersedes the expected-success portion of the prior owner handoff): owner confirmed `./lab-vm auth` starts guest OpenCode and `/connect` opens the host browser, but the callback does not return to the VM. Diagnose the host-loopback → SSH `-L` → guest-listener route and the guest's actual callback listener for the pinned OpenCode method/version; add redacted, URL/code-free diagnostics and a regression before requesting another browser attempt. On the next controlled run verify callback completion, guest `opencode auth list`, and one harmless provider completion. Do not copy/paste or record the authorization URL, state, code, or token; preserve VM/overlay/host-Docker session and do not change firewall/network settings.

Implement workspace-selected auth bootstrap after the TUI first-login milestone: verify the standard `./lab <workspace>`/configured VM start path finds the intended credential without separate manual setup, and document first-run login versus subsequent reuse.

Implement and test recursive credential availability only when recursion is explicitly enabled: one nested Little Mester agent can use the same provider auth via a narrow runtime channel, with no secret in Git, build context, image, seed, logs, or unrestricted parent/child workspace exposure. Verify the minimum one-level nested case and existing recursion depth bounds.

NEXT OWNER TEST after diagnostic patch sync: preserve the running VM/overlay and host-Docker session; run one `./lab-vm -d auth`, then guest `/connect` → OpenAI → browser OAuth. If it fails, exit and report only the redacted OpenCode error plus filtered SSH transport lines using the command recorded on #41; do not share full logs or OAuth data and do not repeat the attempt before reviewing evidence. The trace distinguishes no host callback connection, an SSH guest-listener connect failure, and a callback that reached the guest but failed later during provider exchange. If it succeeds, record only callback result and OpenCode version/method; run the separate auth-list/provider-completion acceptance after success.

SUPERSEDES earlier owner handoffs that mention fixed callback ports 1455/1457 or a static callback tunnel. After this dynamic-forward patch is present in the CachyOS checkout, preserve the current VM/overlay and host-Docker session; do not run up/clean/stop/down or alter firewall/network settings. Run exactly one `./lab-vm -d auth`, then guest `/connect` → OpenAI → browser OAuth. The host bridge should derive the port from the authorize URL's redirect_uri and install one loopback forward before Firefox opens; do not manually copy/share the URL or port. If it fails, exit TUI and return only the redacted error plus filtered transport lines from `grep -E 'forward|listener|open failed|connect_to' .mester/vm/default/browser-bridge-ssh.log`; do not share the full log or OAuth URL/state/code/token, and do not retry before review. If it succeeds, report callback result/version/method, make one harmless OpenAI completion, then confirm guest `opencode auth list` reports OpenAI stored. Do not tear down VM/container state.

Before the next owner auth attempt, finish local regressions for source-shaped callback validation, failed/occupied forwarding refusing browser launch, SSH config isolation and temporary-master cleanup, and proxy HTTP/CONNECT rejection of private/link-local/mixed-DNS targets. Record local results separately from real-host acceptance. Do not add api.openai.com or ask for model completion under the current allowlist.

SUPERSEDES earlier owner handoffs that require an OpenAI provider completion as part of browser login. First complete the #41 `models status` check after reported proxy reload, then one `./lab-vm -d auth` browser login using `/connect` → OpenAI → Sign in with ChatGPT. Acceptance here is callback plus `opencode auth list` only; current `.mester-egress` intentionally denies api.openai.com, so do not try model completion or broaden policy without explicit owner approval. Preserve existing VM/overlay/host-Docker auth; no --clean/stop/down/container recreation. Share only redacted error and filtered SSH forwarding lines on failure, never OAuth material. Test cancellation cleanup separately after success.

SUPERSEDES the earlier owner handoff command `./lab-vm -d auth`: the only TUI command is now `./lab-vm -d agent --browser-auth` for browser OAuth (`./lab-vm agent` for normal direct guest use). Preserve the running VM/overlay, host-Docker session and credentials; do not run up --clean, stop, down, recreate containers, or change firewall/egress. First run `./lab-vm models status`; if healthy, run exactly one `./lab-vm -d agent --browser-auth`, then guest `/connect` → OpenAI → **Sign in with ChatGPT** and verify `opencode auth list`. Do not attempt a completion because api.openai.com remains unapproved. On failure share only the redacted error and filtered SSH transport lines, never OAuth URL/state/code/token. No retry before review.

It is a separate, user-controlled helper, not an always-on QEMU forward.

2026-10-29 callback implementation correction: source commit 1097e2668b1e08ad63bdf0b1c4860b9bc01e420c for pinned OpenCode 2.2.0 (`packages/core/src/plugin/provider/chatgpt.ts`) binds an ephemeral callback with `server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1")` and uses that port in `redirect_uri`; this is source-level behavior, not a documented CLI/API guarantee. Host MCP bridge now extracts only the validated redirect_uri port and requests exactly one `127.0.0.1:<port>` → guest `127.0.0.1:<port>` control-master forward before opening the original URL. It fails closed for unexpected callback shape/forward failure. Tests cover 40391 extraction, invalid URI rejection, loopback-only SSH args, idempotence and forward-before-open. `docs/DECISIONS.md` C.9.13, `docs/vm-architecture.md`, `docs/chatgpt-auth.md` and README document the source dependency and version-bump revalidation.

Architecture clarification 2026-10-28: native OpenAI/OpenCode browser sign-in is required in the guest itself; host credential escrow/import is optional convenience and must not turn the guest into a containerized agent or substitute legacy device-code/API-key auth for the required browser flow.
